title: La historia de mis abuelos
blurbEn: The last text of the unit: a whole life told in the preterite, which is exactly what this tense is for.
body:
Mis abuelos se conocieron en mil novecientos sesenta, en una fiesta de pueblo.

Mi abuelo la vio y no dijo nada durante toda la noche. Al final ella se acercó y le preguntó su nombre.

Se casaron dos años después. Vivieron primero en Madrid, pero no les gustó la ciudad y volvieron al pueblo.

Allí nacieron mis tíos y mi madre.

Mi abuelo trabajó cuarenta años en el campo. Mi abuela abrió una tienda pequeña en la plaza y la llevó hasta el año pasado.

Todavía viven en la misma casa.
translationEn:
My grandparents met in nineteen sixty, at a village party.

My grandfather saw her and said nothing all evening. In the end she came over and asked him his name.

They married two years later. They lived in Madrid first, but they did not like the city and went back to the village.

My uncles and my mother were born there.

My grandfather worked forty years in the countryside. My grandmother opened a small shop in the square and ran it until last year.

They still live in the same house.

conocieron.note: 'conocer' in the preterite means *met for the first time*, not *knew*. The tense changes the meaning of the verb itself.

vio.note: Short and irregular. No accent, unlike most he/she preterites.

nacieron.note: Spanish uses an active verb here where English uses a passive: they 'were born' is literally 'they born-ed'.

phrases.note: Spanish reads years as full numbers: 'one thousand nine hundred sixty', never as two pairs.
